script: "She screamed: 'This Sprite is lemon‑lime—what's you store hiding?'". It was scorching—like, the sun was a full‑on sauna, and my garden store felt like a greenhouse on fire. We kept a fridge with drinks right by the front counter because people were dying for a cold sip. A woman walks in, all thirsty, and asks if we have Sprite. I point her to the fridge, like, "Here, the usual ones." She pulls out a can, opens it, and goes, "Bruh, this Sprite is lemon‑lime! It's not normal Sprite!" I look at her, like, "Uh… that's the default Sprite flavor?" "No, it's not. Sprite is Sprite flavored." I've been drinking Sprite since forever, and I am fairly certain it's always been lemon‑lime. (Literally, it's a lemon‑lime soda, not some weird "sprite" taste.) I am like, "Okay, if you want it, here's your can." She nods, takes it, doesn't open it in front of me, but I can already imagine her face when she tastes it and realizes it's just regular Sprite—no surprise, no drama. I didn't even know how to react. I just shrugged and said, "Sure thing." I wish I'd been there to see her reaction, but it was a hot day, and the store was buzzing. The whole thing was just a quick, awkward moment—no big deal, just another day in the life of a garden store clerk who knows the difference between real Sprite and the "lemon‑lime" label.
